data.body: Story A (4143) claimed after the C+D land (fresh review-plan at the default ref: PASS, 0 blocking) and implemented via held-out TDD. RED first: 28 tests, 26 failed for the right reasons (script absent, settings has no hooks key, script untracked). I caught two VACUOUS passes at RED - the line-cap test and the non-Bash test were trivially green because an absent script emits nothing - and tightened the line-cap test to require a non-empty message so emptiness cannot satisfy a cap. Held out 27 tests; implementer (standard tier / sonnet, separate subagent) saw only the happy path and reported green on attempt 1, and independently narrowed its exception handling to satisfy ruff BLE001. Full held-out oracle: 35/36, the single miss being the git-tracked assertion which was mine to satisfy (the implementer was told not to commit); after staging, 28/28 GREEN. TEETH CHECK - 5 mutations, all caught by the right test: (1) removing grep/rg/egrep/fgrep from the trigger -> 12 RED; (2) adding permissionDecision 'allow' -> the non-blocking test RED; (3) returning 2 instead of 0 on malformed JSON -> the robustness test RED; (4) stripping the string-literal exception from the message -> the never-misleading test RED; (5) unwiring the hook from .claude/settings.json -> the wiring test RED. Refactoring litmus: every assertion is on observable behaviour (stdout JSON envelope, exit code, file state) and none names an internal symbol, so a rename or extraction inside the script would not break them. make lint + make typecheck clean; full suite running.
